lessons.title: Back and Forth: The World Oscillates
lessons.focus: Swings, pendulums, springs, branches, guitar strings; define cycle, period, frequency, amplitude.
lessons.advanced: A pendulum makes 20 cycles in 25 s: compute period and frequency with units.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a Pendulum
lessons.focus: Bob, string, pivot; equilibrium position; restoring force grows with displacement; energy sloshes PE↔KE.
lessons.advanced: Sketch force arrows at both extremes and at the bottom; where is speed greatest and why?

lessons.title: Timing a Pendulum Properly
lessons.focus: Time 10 swings and divide; start at 'zero' at the fastest point; why single-swing timing lies.
lessons.advanced: Ten swings: 19.8, 20.2, 20.0 s. Give period with uncertainty and explain the 10-swing gain.

lessons.title: What Affects the Period? Test: Mass
lessons.focus: Same length, stone vs wooden bob: no change; fair-test discipline; Galileo's cathedral story.
lessons.advanced: Explain mass-independence using both F=ma and the PE↔KE exchange.

lessons.title: What Affects the Period? Test: Amplitude
lessons.focus: Small vs large swings: nearly equal (small-angle magic); where it breaks down (>30°).
lessons.advanced: Measure period at 10°, 30°, 60°: quantify the breakdown and explain the small-angle approximation.

lessons.title: What Affects the Period? Test: Length — The One That Matters
lessons.focus: Vary length 20–100 cm; period grows; collect the class dataset for the graph lesson.
lessons.advanced: Predict the period at 25 cm given 1.0 s at 100 cm, using T∝√L.

lessons.title: The Pendulum Graph: T² Against L
lessons.focus: Plot T² vs L: a straight line through origin; gradient = 4π²/g; compute g from your own graph.
lessons.advanced: Full computation: gradient 0.040 s²/cm → g in m/s²; compare with your Unit 4 drop result.

lessons.title: Measuring g Precisely: Pendulum vs Drop
lessons.focus: Compare pendulum and drop methods side by side; which is more accurate and why; repeatability.
lessons.advanced: Write an error budget for both methods; recommend the school-standard procedure.

lessons.title: Build: The One-Second Pendulum Clock I
lessons.focus: Build a stand and pendulum; target T=1.00 s; compute the needed length (≈25 cm) then approach it by tuning.
lessons.advanced: Use T=2π√(L/g) to predict L for T=1.000 s at g=9.8; compare with your tuned result.
